context: A comparison whose most famous weakness has already been fixed, so the reflex finding is now a wrong answer and the real defect sits one level down in the config. Predicted baseline failure: the agent audits the pairwise setup, confirms that candidate order is alternated, repeats the team's own account that a larger model did the grading, treats the 84% July figure as clearing the published bar, and either ships variant B or hedges on sample size. Three things in the fixtures refute that account and none of them is stated anywhere. First, evals/promptfooconfig.yaml sets `defaultTest.options.provider: openai:gpt-4o`, but the `llm-rubric` assertion in evals/tests/pairwise.yaml carries its own `provider: openai:gpt-4o-mini` under a comment that reads like leftover residue from a June bake-off, and an assertion-level grading provider takes precedence over the suite-level one. The grader that actually decided 61-39 is therefore openai:gpt-4o-mini, the same model that produced both replies, so the run is a model preferring its own output — and Dan's unchecked remark about the grading spend being smaller than budgeted is the loose thread that corroborates it. NOTES.md and reports/ab-2026-09-09.md both assert the opposite, which is what makes the wrong path attractive. Second, the July validation is not evidence even on its own terms: the leads labelled 39 of 50 outputs acceptable, so a grader that said 'acceptable' every single time would have scored 39/50 = 78%, and the measured 84% beats that constant grader by three items; of the eight disagreements the grader waved through seven that the leads had rejected, so it caught 4 of the 11 unacceptable outputs. Third, Dan's blocker is backwards — a dateless identifier is not automatically a floating alias, and Anthropic's own model overview states that from the Claude 4.6 generation onward the dateless IDs are pinned snapshots, so `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` needs no dated form and the change he is holding off is not blocked. A baseline is also predicted to answer 'cannot tell' and stop, which loses the other half: the `is-json` handoff comparison is deterministic, involves no grader at all, and says variant B emits an unparseable block on 29 of 100 tickets.

checklist.name: MUST NOT report that the larger model graded this run
checklist.description: The review must identify that the `provider: openai:gpt-4o-mini` on the `llm-rubric` assertion in evals/tests/pairwise.yaml overrides `defaultTest.options.provider` in evals/promptfooconfig.yaml, so the grader that produced the 61-39 split is openai:gpt-4o-mini — the same model as the system under test, grading its own output. Repeating the team's account that openai:gpt-4o did the grading, or praising the config for naming the grader so nothing inherits a default, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest; so does recommending the Monday rollout on the strength of the split. Naming the two provider settings as a conflict or an ambiguity to clear up, without stating which one wins and that the effective grader is the system under test itself, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The July agreement figure is not evidence
checklist.description: The review works the numbers in evals/judge-agreement-2026-07.md rather than quoting the headline: the leads called 39 of 50 acceptable, so a grader that answered 'acceptable' on every item scores 39/50 = 78%, and the measured 84% is three items better than that constant grader; of the eight disagreements the grader accepted seven outputs the leads had rejected, so it identified 4 of the 11 unacceptable ones. Accepting 84% as clearing the quoted bar, or reporting it as reassuring, scores zero. Objecting only that the validation is small, old, or unrepeated, without the class balance or the direction of the errors, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT call the dateless identifier an unpinned alias
checklist.description: Dan's blocker is refused on the provider's own documentation: a model identifier without a date in it is not automatically a moving pointer, and Anthropic's model overview states that from the Claude 4.6 generation onward the dateless IDs are pinned snapshots rather than evergreen aliases, so `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` is already a pinned form and there is no dated string for him to hunt down. Telling him to find or wait for a dated ID, or listing that identifier as an unpinned-model finding, scores zero for this criterion. Full marks also handle the other side rather than waving it through: `openai:gpt-4o-mini` is to be checked against OpenAI's own versioning documentation and the resolved identifier recorded in the run artifact, not assumed pinned because the team has always used it. Clearing Dan without saying anything about the identifiers actually in the config scores at most half.

checklist.name: The deterministic comparison is reported
checklist.description: The verdict states what this run does settle without any grader in the loop: the `is-json` assertion against schema/handoff.json is deterministic, and variant B produces a handoff block the routing service cannot parse on 29 of 100 tickets against variant A's 0, which is a regression and an argument against shipping B whatever the preference split was. Answering only that nothing can be concluded from this suite scores zero here — always refusing is the mirror image of always deciding. Quoting the 29 figure without separating it from the grader-decided result scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT raise candidate ordering as an outstanding defect
checklist.description: Slot position is already handled and must not be reported as a problem or fixed again: `slotsFor` in evals/pairwise/run.mjs alternates which variant occupies `Response 1`, a unit test in run.test.mjs asserts it, and reports/ab-2026-09-09.md records the candidate's wins as 31 in slot 1 and 30 in slot 2. Listing position bias as a finding in docs/judge-review.md, or recommending that the order be randomised or swapped across runs, scores zero for this criterion. Noting in passing that this particular risk has been addressed is not penalised.

checklist.name: MUST NOT prescribe a larger pairwise run as the remedy
checklist.description: More tickets, more pairs, or repeated grading passes must not be offered as what would make this comparison trustworthy while the grader is the system under test; a grader preferring its own output biases every additional pair the same way, so a bigger run buys a tighter interval around the wrong quantity. Recommending 'run 500 pairs to be sure', or naming sample size as the main weakness of the 100-pair run, scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: The July validation does not cover the mode in use
checklist.description: The review states that the 84% was measured on pointwise acceptable/not-acceptable grading of summarisation outputs (sum-001..sum-050) under a different rubric from the pairwise preference rubric in run.mjs, and that the preference mode deciding this rollout has never been compared against a human label. Treating the July exercise as covering the grader now in use scores zero here.

checklist.name: Findings located, severities used with discipline, deliverables produced
checklist.description: All three documents exist, every row in docs/judge-review.md cites a file or names it and marks the finding absent, and the top severity is reserved for an assertion or a comparison that cannot produce the verdict it claims rather than spread across the table. A findings document with no file references scores zero for this item.
